title: Flow-controlled tiled pagination and cursor coalescing for dashboard query API
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Certain Dashboard explorations with deep pagination (offsets > 10k) and mixed hot/cold tenant distributions cause high tail latency and excessive read amplification on our analytics store. Existing cursor pagination sometimes generates many small backend queries and duplicates index traversals for overlapping time windows.

Goal: Implement a tiled pagination layer and cursor coalescing strategy in the Dashboard query API that reduces backend query count, stabilizes 95/99th percentile latency for large cursors, and lowers CPU/IO cost per page for heavy queries. Target: 30-40% reduction in backend query count for long-range paginated views and 20% reduction in 99th percentile latency on heavy tenant workloads (based on current benchmarks).

Scope: API layer changes in console-backend that govern pagination cursors and request framing, query planner hints to the analytics pipeline for tile-aligned scans, and a lightweight cache for recent tiles and coalesced cursor ranges. Does NOT include reworking materialized views or storage engine changes; will integrate with existing shard-aware prefix caching and index hints.

Non-goals: Full rewrite of dashboard query planner, adding new materialized aggregated tables, or changing tenant data retention.

Risks: Additional complexity in cursor format, compatibility with older clients (we will provide backward-compatible fallback to legacy cursors), potential cache invalidation issues during rollouts.

Success metrics: backend query count per paginated request, 95/99th latency, CPU and IO consumed per paginated-heavy dashboard workload, and no increase in error rate or incorrect results during A/B rollout.
acceptance_criteria: API returns stable opaque cursors that encode tiled ranges and can be decoded by server for coalescing
A/B rollout shows >=30% reduction in backend query count for long-range pagination on synthetic heavy tenant tests
95th and 99th percentile latency for affected dashboards reduced by >=15% and >=20% respectively in staging benchmarks
Rollback path exists: legacy cursors accepted and routing toggled via feature flag without client changes
Integration tests covering tile cache invalidation, concurrent cursor advancement, and cross-shard coalescing pass in CI
implementation_notes: Introduce tiled pagination: split time/sequence ranges into fixed-size tiles (configurable by route) and expose cursors that point to (tile_id, offset_within_tile)
Cursor coalescing: when multiple near-consecutive cursors are observed from a client/session, merge requests server-side into a single tile fetch where safe to reduce duplicate work
Server-side flow control: limit concurrent tile fetches per-tenant and prioritize small-page low-latency requests to stay within SLOs; fall back to single-tile mode under contention
Cache: implement an in-memory LRU tile cache scoped per-console-node with configurable TTL and a small hot-tenant fast-path; use Leases to avoid thundering herds on cache miss
Indexing hints: pass tile-aligned index ranges to analytics service to enable targeted shard scans and avoid full time-window index scans
Backward compatibility: add feature-flagged cursor versioning and a transparent conversion layer for older cursors to legacy behavior
Instrumentation: add counters for tile hits/misses, coalesced-request count, per-request backend query count, and metrics for cache contention to Console metrics and Grafana dashboards
Rollout plan: start with internal tenants in staging, then canary 5% of production tenants (non-enterprise) for two days, monitor success metrics and error rates, then expand to 50% and full rollout
progress_updates: 2025-01-11: Kickoff meeting - agreed tiled size default 1h for time-indexed dashboards and parameterizable per-route. Action: Mateo to prototype cursor encoding format.
2025-01-15: Prototype implemented for cursor format + server decode/encode. Local bench: single-node synthetic workload shows 28% fewer backend queries for 50-page scans.
2025-01-17: Design review - PM (Liam Chen) requested explicit rollback feature flag and clearer migration notes for SDKs. Added feature-flag plan and compatibility docs link.

2025-01-20: Bench in staging with multi-tenant distribution: 32% backend query reduction, 18% 99th latency reduction on heavy tenant sample (pre-optimization of cache TTL). Identified cache eviction thrash for some tenants -> tuning required.

2025-01-23: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/console-backend/pull/1987 implementing cursor layer and basic tile cache (draft). Seeking eng review from storage team and infra for lease semantics.
